item.title: Price adequacy is essential as ILS expands into casualty, specialty, and cyber: Artex’s Faries
item.description: As the ILS market expands its reach across casualty, specialty, and cyber, maintaining price adequacy remains a critical boundary for market growth. I think we have to watch the price adequacy and the softening to make sure that we don’t dip below a threshold that will cause investors to think about whether to deploy their capital elsewhere, but I don’t think we’re there yet.” As the ILS space continues to tap into hybrid, casualty, and specialty structures, operational complexity is also rising sharply. But it’s always a supply, demand, and return equation.” Turning to casualty, Faries explained that she sees sustained momentum ahead, adding: “Overall, I think there is further opportunity in casualty so we expect that growth to continue into 2027.” On specialty lines, Faries pointed to key market mechanisms facilitating institutional capital deployment: “Regarding specialty, we are involved in London Bridge 2 in the UK, which is the vehicle that efficiently delivers capital supporting Lloyd’s Syndicates.

item.title: Swiss Re expects to remain a meaningful participant in alternative capital: Baertschi
item.description: Speaking today at Swiss Re’s briefing at RVS 2026 in Monte Carlo, Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer, of P&C Reinsurance, underscored the importance of the reinsurers third-party capital markets focused Alternative Capital Partners (ACP) division, and stated that Swiss Re expects to continue to be a “meaningful participant in that market.” During Swiss Re’s media briefing at RVS today, Baertschi stressed the overall importance of the reinsurance industry having a strong capital base. The rest we think of as alternative capital as well.” Baertschi continued: “Alternative capital is an important part of the capital stack, and the opportunities that insurance companies and buyers of this kind of protection have, and it also very importantly supports the traditional reinsurance capacity.” In light of this, we asked senior executives what the reinsurer’s plans were for growing its Alternative Capital Partners division into 2027. Earlier this year, Swiss Re launched a new Alternative Capital Solutions unit to encompass its activities in ILS and retrocessional hedging and execution.

item.title: Cat bonds and casualty sidecars buoyant, but investors still don’t like surprises: Josefs, S&P
item.description: At the S&P Global Ratings briefing in Monte Carlo at the RVS, Maren Josefs, Credit Analyst at the company explained that the big stories in insurance-linked securities has been catastrophe bonds and casualty sidecars this year, but she cautioned the market to remember that investors still don’t like surprises. The protection gap between economic and insured losses is still widening across the globe, and at the same time, we have these new risks coming from geopolitics, climate, and technology advances, especially AI.” Moving on Josefs highlighted the two biggest sources of growth, as catastrophe bonds and reinsurance sidecars. Josefs stated, “The two main stories have been the cat bond market and the sidecars, especially on the casualty side.

item.title: Moody’s warns uncertainty around emerging risks could constrain re/insurance growth
item.description: “Insurers may want to tap into growth in emerging markets or new areas of risk, but uncertainty is high, and too many insurers don’t have the tools to understand the risks and grow meaningfully into these new areas.” Speaking at their firm’s briefing in Monte Carlo today, Brandan Holmes, SVP at Moody’s Ratings, and Joe Melly, Head of Casualty and Financial Lines at Moody’s Insurance Solutions, warned that insurers are navigating an increasingly interconnected and uncertain emerging-risk landscape. In his opening remarks at the briefing, held at the 68th edition of the Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS), Holmes suggested that the centre of gravity on insurance emerging risks is shifting.

item.title: Compre completes retrospective structured ADC transaction with Lloyd’s syndicate
item.description: Compre Group Holdings Limited (Compre), the Bermuda-domiciled international specialty reinsurance group, has reached an agreement on a retrospective structured adverse development cover (ADC) transaction with a Lloyd’s syndicate. Rachel Bardon, Chief Underwriting Officer at Compre, said, “This transaction is a strong example of how we are continuing to evolve our retrospective proposition to meet clients’ changing capital and balance sheet needs. The transaction covers the syndicate’s 2023 and prior Years of Account on a whole-account basis, spanning a multi-line portfolio of property and casualty business and assumed reinsurance, with subject reserves of approximately £200 million.

item.title: Closing cyber protection gap a major business opportunity: Munich Re
item.description: Speaking during the firm’s briefing at the 2026 Rendez-Vous de Septembre (RVS) in Monte Carlo, Stefan Golling, a Member of the Board of Management of Munich Re, suggested that the industry has not done enough to close the significant cyber protection gap, while also flagging the major business opportunity in doing so as Munich Re looks to maintain its position as a market leader in the growing sector. He went on, “Closing the cyber protection gap is a major business opportunity, but it’s also our responsibility as an industry if we want to live up to the picture of being the immune system for our customers. Golling observed that much of the growth in cyber has come over the past 24 to 36 months and, with rates having softened, said he believes the industry has not done enough to close the significant protection gap.

item.title: Experian launches credit card app on ChatGPT
item.description: Experian has launched a credit card shopping app on ChatGPT, allowing users to discover and compare offers from its partner network without leaving the conversation. Those who want personalized offers are redirected to Experian, where members can view cards matched to their credit profile, including eligible preapproved and No Ding Decline offers. The launch expands Experian’s use of conversational AI across loans, insurance and credit cards.

item.title: domusIQ launches UK real estate MGA
item.description: Commercial real estate analytics platform domusIQ has launched a global insurance business and begun underwriting through a new UK MGA. The MGA will target commercial real estate, residential and commercial property owners, and commercial combined risks. domusIQ MGA (UK), hosted on the Davies MGA Services platform, began underwriting on August 1.

item.title: Simply Business renews Premium Credit partnership
item.description: Simply Business and Premium Credit have renewed their insurance financing partnership under a six-year agreement. Premium Credit will continue to support Simply Business through its finance platform and API integration, allowing customers to finance their insurance premiums. Simply Business serves small businesses and landlords in the UK.

item.title: El mercado blando en reaseguro continuará
item.description: El mercado de reaseguro afronta los últimos meses de 2026 con precios en descenso, respaldados por buenos resultados y un capital elevado. El entorno externo se mantiene inestable, con primas de riesgo de renta variable y costes de financiación al alza, junto a incertidumbre económica y geopolítica.

item.title: La inversión en infraestructuras estratégicas abre al reaseguro una demanda inédita de cobertura
item.description: Swiss Re Institute estima que las inversiones en centros de datos de inteligencia artificial y en energías renovables podrían generar unos 200.000 millones de dólares en primas de seguro comercial acumuladas entre 2026 y 2030, según un informe presentado este sábado con motivo del Rendez-Vous de Septembre.

item.title: Insurance Claims Lose the Paper Chase as AI Gets to Work
item.description: Insurance claims have always been document-heavy, time-sensitive, and prone to fraud. A Swiss Re article written by Florian Maurer, chief D&T officer Corporate Solutions, and Vincent Plantard, GL head of Performance, Analytics and Delivery at Claims Corporate Solutions, describes how SwissRe built and deployed ClaimsGenAI to automate its corporate insurance claims handling process. SwissRe’s annual corporate insurance claims now exceed 40,000, creating a clear need for a step change in how the company manages growing caseloads.

item.title: Hannover Re on steady ILS growth path with Capital Partners after first capital raise: Silke Sehm
item.description: “HCP has successfully written additional non-proportional catastrophe business in 2026 under its first third-party capital mandate, so we are on a steady growth path within our broader ILS offering framework.” Regarding how much capital was raised, Sehm said it was a “lower three-digit million number” Michael Eberhardt, CEO Hannover Re Capital Partners and Head of P&C, Hannover Re Bermuda, said: “Yes, so we are fully aligned with the investor base, and also we have a governance structure around it. Speaking in Monte Carlo this morning, Hannover Re Executive Board Member Silke Sehm noted that the company’s ILS management platform, Hannover Re Capital Partners, successfully wrote additional non-proportional catastrophe business in 2026 under its first third-party capital mandate, with a “lower three-digit million number” of capital raised. Recall that the global reinsurer launched its Hannover Re Capital Partners operation at the beginning of 2026 and in advance of that had explained the rationale as putting in place a missing piece of Hannover Re’s ILS offering .

item.title: ILS will return to the cyber conversation in time. AI risk a future factor: Baker, CyberCube
item.description: Speaking with Artemis around the time of the Monte Carlo Reinsurance Rendez-vous event, Baker said that investor engagement on understanding cyber risk and readying themselves to invest in the cyber ILS asset class continues. Baker of CyberCube explained why the cyber cat bond market has been quiet of late, highlighting the economics, “The soft market means traditional reinsurance capacity exists at lower prices, which decreases the general need to reach towards the ILS market for risk and capital management. “On top of that, cyber balance sheets are not yet a significant driver in a lot of carrier or reinsurance companies’ overall risk, so time and resources get spent elsewhere first right now.” She continued to say that investor interest is not a limiting factor, “That said, from what we can see there is more investor demand than sponsor supply, so that’s not holding back the market at this time.

item.title: Catastrophe bond fund UCITS Index delivers 1.24% average return in August: Plenum
item.description: Catastrophe bond fund structured in the UCITS investment format delivered their strongest month of performance year-to-date through the August days of record, averaging 1.24% for the period, while the 12-month rolling return average across the Plenum CAT Bond UCITS Fund Indices slipped a little further to 9.82%. The average return of UCITS catastrophe bond funds is the strongest so far in 2026 for a reporting period, since the nearest last end of month reporting of this Index, on July 31st through to August 28th 2026, at 1.24%. On the back of this, the average year-to-date performance of the UCITS catastrophe bond fund strategies rose from 4.09 % as of July 31st, to now 5.38% as of August 28th 2026.

item.title: PwC RVS: Convex’s Brand says strong carriers can thrive in soft phase of cycle
item.description: Speaking at PwC’s annual breakfast briefing during this year’s RVS in Monte Carlo, Paul Brand, Chief Executive Officer of international specialty insurer and reinsurer Convex, suggested that carriers with relevance, resilience and efficiency do absolutely fine during this phase of the cycle. Rather than viewing softer conditions as a uniform challenge, Brand suggested that the cycle tends to expose differences in the quality and positioning of carriers. “The very interesting thing about the soft phase of the cycle is that this is the point in time when outcomes actually disperse.

item.title: Underlying need for reinsurance protection continues to grow: Swiss Re
item.description: Urs Baertschi, Chief Executive Officer, Property & Casualty Reinsurance, Swiss Re, commented, “The underlying need for protection continues to grow as the risk landscape evolves and becomes more interconnected. According to Swiss Re’s modelled scenarios, insured losses could reach around USD 320 billion in a 2026 peak loss scenario, highlighting that reinsurance protection against low-frequency, high-severity events is important. At the 68th annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Swiss Re, an industry giant, has emphasised that growing natural catastrophe risk remains a significant driver of reinsurance demand.

item.title: Cyber reinsurance buyers willing to explore higher cessions at Jan 1 renewals: Marsh Re’s Cordonnier
item.description: Anthony Cordonnier, Global Co-Head of Cyber, Managing Director at reinsurance broker Marsh Re, said a meaningful shift that is beginning to appear is a willingness among some buyers to explore higher cessions at the 1 January 2027 cyber renewals. In an interview with Reinsurance News around the annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Cordonnier explained that buyers of cyber reinsurance are exploring higher cessions as they reassess whether their current programmes are appropriately sized for the risks they are running. At the key 1.1 2027 cyber renewals, Cordonnier noted that buyers with the widest range of options are likely to be those that have invested properly in understanding their exposure and can articulate a coherent underwriting strategy to the market.

item.title: Viewpoint: How the Federal Ban on Intoxicating Hemp Products Will Reshape Risk and Coverage
item.description: I have been writing about the insurance risks of intoxicating hemp products since 2021, when delta-8 THC gummies first started showing up in convenience stores and gas stations across the country. There is real momentum behind some of these efforts, and even the White House has signaled support for protecting non-intoxicating hemp products from the ban’s overreach. These products violate the spirit, if not the actual letter, of the 2018 Farm Bill, and the cannabis and hemp industries and their insurers should be wary of a government response.

item.title: Amwins acquires firearms insurance MGA
item.description: Amwins has acquired Joseph Chiarello & Co., a Summit, New Jersey-based MGA specializing in commercial insurance for the firearms industry. Its program provides commercial package, umbrella and general liability coverage to firearms manufacturers, distributors, retailers, shooting clubs, instructors, and ammunition and accessory manufacturers. The business has spent more than 40 years focused on the firearms industry and carries an endorsement from the National Shooting Sports Foundation.

item.title: Third-party capital remains an attractive source of capital for SCOR: CEO Léger
item.description: Speaking at global reinsurer SCOR’s briefing at RVS 2026 in Monte Carlo, Thierry Léger, Chief Executive Officer (CEO) said that the reinsurer sees third-party capital as an attractive source of capital for the firm, and sees no future changes regarding its strategy for managing it. “We see third-party capital for SCOR as an attractive source of capital, given our brand is very strong. French reinsurer SCOR is an active manager of third-party capital through its asset management subsidiary, SCOR Investment Partners, and dedicated risk partnership initiatives.

item.title: Brian Lewis named Chief Financial Officer of Aspida Life Re
item.description: Aspida Holdings, a provider of retirement and reinsurance solutions, has announced the appointment of Brian Lewis as Chief Financial Officer of Aspida Life Re. “Brian brings an exceptional combination of technical expertise, strategic perspective, and deep knowledge of the Bermuda reinsurance market,” said David Florian, Chief Executive Officer of Aspida Re. In his new position, Lewis will leverage his 13 years of leadership experience across reinsurance finance, capital management, and regulatory reporting, to oversee the financial operations of Aspida Re, a Bermuda-based reinsurance platform.

item.title: SCOR leans into AI as reinsurer warns of governance and liability challenges
item.description: Speaking at a media briefing held during the Monte Carlo Rendez-Vous, SCOR’s Group Chief Executive Officer, Thierry Léger, and the Chief Executive Officer of SCOR Global P&C, Jean-Paul Conoscente, set out the reinsurer’s view on the forces reshaping the industry, with artificial intelligence (AI) emerging as one of the most significant themes of the discussion. “At SCOR, we are totally leaning into AI. “Personally, I see one of the biggest challenges in AI coming from governance,” he said, pointing to the emergence of “agentic AI-driven people, if you want virtual employees,” that are beginning to support underwriting decisions and may, in time, make them independently.

item.title: EQT to Pay $2 Billion for Majority Stake in McGill and Partners
item.description: EQT AB has agreed to acquire a majority stake in UK insurance broker McGill and Partners from Warburg Pincus LLC for $2 billion, as the Swedish buyout firm looks to accelerate the company’s global expansion. Founded in 2019, McGill and Partners has grown to more than 600 employees across seven countries, generating revenue of more than $250 million. Founder and Chief Executive Officer Steve McGill will continue to lead the business, while Chairman John Lloyd will remain actively involved.

item.description: Investors backing insurance-linked securities funds under the management of Cedar Trace Capital Management are expected to provide some of the capital to support the planned launch of a $300m Lloyd’s syndicate for the 2027 underwriting year, by group company Cedar Trace Underwriting. Holden added, “Lloyd’s is obviously a market that David and I know extremely well and the capital and licensing advantages that it brings allow us to expand our offerings to our existing reinsurance relationships and to bring new delegated coverholders to the market.” Lorraine Harfitt, CEO, Asta, who will provide managing agency and associated services to the syndicate, stated, “We are delighted to support Cedar Trace as it establishes its Lloyd’s platform. Existing shareholders of affiliated insurer Mereo Insurance is expected to be the main source of capital to support the Cedar Trace Underwriting syndicate at Lloyd’s.

item.title: Capital inflows, low cat losses to pressure Jan 1 rates, structural integrity the focus in ILS: Twelve Securis
item.description: An influx of capital inflows and low catastrophe losses are likely to pressure rates at the upcoming January renewals, which leads Twelve Securis’ Cahal Doris to note that structural integrity will remain a key focus for the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market during the key season. All of which leads the CIO to note that structural integrity remains a key focus for ILS. In a market that is expected to soften absent any catastrophes, the managers that have access to a broad range of opportunities are best placed.” Sticking with the January renewals, Doris explained that he believes competitive pressure will likely remain a feature of the ILS market if catastrophe activity continues to remain manageable and capital also continues to be abundant.

item.title: Munich Re execs caution on casualty sidecar commutation challenge, risky asset strategies
item.description: In Monte Carlo today at the Rendez-vous event, senior executives of global reinsurance firm Munich Re explained that they see the trend for some longer-tailed casualty focused sidecars to offer high returns from the asset side as “not a good idea” while the potential for commutation discussions to prove a challenge at the end of a sidecar term was also discussed. Munich Re hosted a media briefing in Monte Carlo and Thomas Blunck and Stefan Golling, both members of the board of management, seem equally against sidecars that have a significant focus on generating returns from the investment side, as well as on those targeting U.S casualty or liability risks. Blunck, who has oversight of Munich Re’s reinsurance division at the board level, commented first, “Another element that I’d like to pinpoint is some of the solutions, for example sidecars that we’re seeing in the alternative space, are taking obviously more asset risk.

item.title: AXA XL Re cautious ahead of Jan renewals, but aims to provide consistent pricing and appetite through the cycle: CEO Guidée
item.description: Global reinsurer AXA XL Re is cautious heading into the key January 1 2027 renewals as there’s still time for meaningful loss events to impact the industry, but in a market with improved discipline, the focus is on providing consistency of pricing and appetite through the cycle, according to CEO Renaud Guidée. “For both property and casualty, we aim to provide consistency of pricing and appetite through the cycle,” he added. But the season is not over and we therefore remain cautious heading into the 1/1 renewals,” he said.

item.title: ‘Value of reinsurance has never been more evident’ as risks become more global & volatile: Munich Re
item.description: Thomas Blunck, Member of the Board of Management, Munich Re, said: “The value of reinsurance has never been more evident than it is today. At the 68th annual meeting of the reinsurance industry in Monte Carlo, Munich Re, one of the world’s largest reinsurance companies, underlined the importance of a resilient reinsurance sector as risks are “becoming more global and more volatile.” Munich Re describes reinsurance as society’s immune system, but warns that the industry is facing an abundance of uncertainties from the changing climate, geopolitical tensions, and rapid technological development. “Consequently, such natural hazards are shifting more and more from being primarily ecological risks to economic risks, even though it is not always easy to establish a causal link in the case of heat-related damage,” said Munich Re.

item.title: Protection gap remains ‘huge’ as third-party capital hits $140bn, reports S&P
item.description: Third-party capital now stands at USD $140 billion, up from USD $90 billion five years ago, with roughly USD $65 billion channelled through platforms and just over USD $20 billion through sidecars, the remainder largely made up of private collateralised transactions. That’s a huge protection gap on natural catastrophe losses.” He went on to argue that the sector has several routes to narrow that gap, saying: “The sector continues to have the ability to shrink that gap, being it with own capacity, convergent capital, or with government, so there’s plenty of opportunities for growth.” At the same time, he was careful to stress that “cautiousness and conservatism is key, in particular with regard to changing of these loss patterns.” Turning to newer lines, Bender described cyber as “clearly a growth area, although the growth also has stopped in the last two years because of also a softening market environment and also a cautious approach from the sector,” adding that “we believe that line of business will have above average growth rates in the next years, and the reinsurance sector can play a significant role in that context.” The most striking example he raised, though, was the exposure now building up around data centres and hyperscalers. It is against this backdrop of expanding capacity that Josefs framed the industry’s central challenge: “The protection gap between economic and insured losses is still widening across the globe, and at the same time we have these new risks coming from geopolitics, climate, and technology advances, especially AI.” Bender picked up the theme directly, confirming just how wide that gap remains on the natural catastrophe side.

item.title: Staying disciplined on underwriting worth up to seven points of return on capital: PwC
item.description: The critical importance of underwriting discipline in reinsurance and insurance-linked securities (ILS) is laid bare in new analysis from PwC, with the company suggesting that remaining strict on terms, conditions and structures could be worth up to seven points of return on capital. The conclusion is that “underwriting discipline matters” PwC said, with a scenario where discipline holds and firms maintain their return thresholds, constraining or redirecting capacity where pricing becomes inadequate, and the combined ratio remains at around 91% and return on capital (RoC) at around 13-14%. Those structural advantages gained through the hard market should not be taken for granted, PwC explained, as looking ahead returns generated will rely “not only on market conditions, but on how effectively firms translate their underwriting strategies into pricing, portfolio management, capital allocation and incentive structures as competitive pressures intensify.” Andy Moore, PwC’s London Market Leader, commented, “The industry has spent years investing in underwriting controls, analytics and governance.

item.title: ILS success hinges on discipline, avoiding past renewal mistakes: Albertini, Leadenhall
item.description: Following a sharp surge in momentum across the insurance-linked securities (ILS) space in recent years, further success in the market hinges on maintaining underwriting discipline and a clear avoidance of past renewal mistakes, Luca Albertini, CEO of Leadenhall Capital Partners LLP, told Artemis in an interview. As year-end renewal negotiations begin taking shape, Albertini explained to Artemis what he believes are the important topics and talking points that ILS markets and alternative capital managers should be taking into their meetings with investors and cedents around the key period. He continued: “There is over $120bn of third-party capital in ILS with a relatively short commitment period and if the industry goes back to past mistakes and loses the trust of its investors and investment advisors, the potential for capital reallocation outside of our space for the medium term can have a material adverse impact on capacity, pricing, terms and conditions for reinsurance buyers for years to come.

item.title: Fitch bullish on ILS momentum, with only “slight” growth forecast for traditional reinsurance capital
item.description: At the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous today, Brian Schneider, Global Head of Reinsurance Ratings at Fitch Ratings seemed more bullish on the insurance-linked securities (ILS) market continuing its recent pace of growth, while traditional reinsurance capital is only forecast for “slight” growth this year. “We do expect slight growth for capital in the full-year 2026.” Then he explained that, “Overall, you can see the traditional capital still dominates, but it is actually declining a bit. Speaking during the Fitch Ratings briefing at the RVS in Monte Carlo this morning, Schneider explained that reinsurance capital levels have continued to grow, but highlighted that ILS expansion means third-party investor capital commands a growing share of the overall.

item.title: ‘Physical economy is back’ as data centres become strategic infrastructure: Swiss Re
item.description: Jérôme Haegeli, Group Chief Economist at Swiss Re and Head of the Swiss Re Institute, has said the “physical economy is back” as the rapid expansion of data centre investment fuels a new global capital expenditure (capex) super-cycle. Swiss Re has said that this investment boom, spanning data centres, energy systems and other strategic infrastructure, could create one of the largest commercial property and casualty (P&C) insurance opportunities in decades . Swiss Re said these investments are transforming data centres from traditional information technology assets into strategic infrastructure, with power requirements measured in gigawatts and asset values running into billions of dollars.

item.title: Cedar Trace obtains in-principle approval from Lloyd’s for new $300m syndicate
item.description: Following in-principle approval from the Lloyd’s Council, Cedar Trace Underwriting has entered the Lloyd’s market with a new $300m syndicate for the 2027 underwriting year, to be led by CUO Richard Holden. The launch of said syndicate is expected to give Cedar Trace an additional source of underwriting capacity and access to Lloyd’s distribution that complements and adds scale to the existing Bermuda platform. Cedar Trace explained that capital supporting the new syndicate is expected to come predominantly from existing shareholders of Mereo Insurance as well as investors supporting Cedar Trace Capital Management’s ILS funds.

item.title: Reinsurer flexibility gives Gallagher Re confidence ahead of Jan 1 renewals: Dowlen, EMEA CEO
item.description: As reinsurers show both flexibility and interest to support the evolving needs of buyers, global reinsurance broker Gallagher Re is confident its clients can achieve good outcomes at the key January 1 renewals, according to Hamish Dowlen, CEO of EMEA. Speaking with Reinsurance News around the 68th edition of RVS in Monte Carlo, Dowlen said that Gallagher Re is “currently very optimistic” for its clients ahead of the key January 1 2027 renewals. While market commentary suggests that reinsurer discipline remains, Dowlen explained that reinsurers are “demonstrating flexibility and interest to support” a variety of possible solutions currently being explored by cedants.

item.title: JRC Insurance joins Leavitt Group
item.description: San Antonio-based JRC Insurance has joined Leavitt Insurance Services of the Rockies. Its clients will continue working with the same team while gaining access to Leavitt Group’s carrier relationships and resources. Leavitt Group operates more than 80 agencies and 290 locations across 31 states.

item.title: Bridge Specialty Group names Todd Wood chief underwriting officer
item.description: Bridge Specialty Group appointed Todd Wood chief underwriting officer for its North American wholesale business. Wood joined Bridge Specialty Group in 2023 through its acquisition of New England Excess Exchange, where he has served as president since 2019. Wood will oversee underwriting strategy, standards and quality controls across the company’s North American operations.

item.title: Capex ‘super-cycle’ among largest commercial P&C opportunities in decades: Swiss Re
item.description: Insurance is essential to making these investments resilient and financeable.” The post Capex ‘super-cycle’ among largest commercial P&C opportunities in decades: Swiss Re appeared first on ReinsuranceNe.ws . A new Swiss Re Institute report has suggested that a global capital expenditure (capex) super-cycle, driven by surging investment in data centres, energy systems and other strategic infrastructure, could create one of the largest commercial property and casualty (P&C) opportunities for insurers in decades. At the same time, the five largest US hyperscalers are expected to invest nearly $800 billion in AI-related capital expenditure in 2026, while estimates for global data-centre capex exceed $1 trillion,” the Swiss Re Institute explained.
